node.label: Theodor W. Adorno
node.date_label: 1944: Philosophical Fragments (limited circulation, with Max Horkheimer) · 1947: Dialectic of Enlightenment (revised publication, with Max Horkheimer) · 1950: The Authoritarian Personality (with Else Frenkel-Brunswik, Daniel J. Levinson and Nevitt Sanford) · 1951: Minima Moralia: Reflexionen aus dem beschädigten Leben · 1966: Negative Dialectics (Negative Dialektik, German original)
node.description: A philosopher, social theorist and critic of music and mass culture associated with the Frankfurt School. With Max Horkheimer he linked standardized cultural production to concentrated economic power; their treatment of amusement and the split between light and serious art complicates a simple opposition between commerce and autonomous culture.

proposed_edges.relationship: With Horkheimer, connects standardized cultural production to economic power rather than autonomous technological necessity.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Joint primary chapter opening read. Authorship is collective; this does not attribute the whole chapter solely to Adorno or adopt its sweeping cultural judgments as findings.

proposed_edges.relationship: With Horkheimer, analyzes amusement’s continuity with work and the historical split between light and serious art.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Joint primary chapter selected later paragraphs read. A conceptual resource for analyzing mass culture, not proof of direct transmission to all British cultural studies or a claim that popular art has no value.
